memory_update.text: Restaurants theme should be tracked as a supply-chain dependency map, not only as a restaurant-operator comp set: demand -> menu-critical inputs -> approved suppliers -> distributors -> logistics/cold chain -> commodity/raw-material constraints.

Frozen potato products/French fries are the highest-priority Layer 1 node because they combine menu profitability, consistency requirements, scale logistics, customer concentration, and a relatively clean public-market mapping through Lamb Weston.

Food-processing equipment for frying, freezing, automation, and inspection is an attractive underfollowed second-order lane because it may benefit from processor modernization even when restaurant brands receive most investor attention.

Cold-chain logistics and foodservice distribution should remain in the universe as infrastructure nodes, but require stronger evidence on foodservice mix, frozen potato exposure, contract structure, and throughput sensitivity.

Sauces, oils, dressings, condiments, and seasonings are important underfollowed restaurant inputs, but direct public-market mapping is currently weak because key cited suppliers such as Ventura Foods and Golden State Foods appear private.

Next layer should verify every ticker's public filings for foodservice revenue purity, named customers, customer concentration, material contracts, commodity pass-through, margins, capacity utilization, and analyst/valuation context.

summary: Merged Layer 1 universe for the Restaurants theme using a Serenity-style supply-chain funnel: restaurant demand and margin pressure are mapped to menu-critical inputs, distributors, cold-chain/logistics infrastructure, processing equipment, B2B beverage platforms, and selected restaurant operators/reference demand anchors. The strongest initial chokepoint lane is frozen potato/French fries, led by Lamb Weston as the purest public-market supplier mapping, with second-order exposure through food-processing equipment, cold storage, distribution, frying oils, and irrigation. The second useful lane is sauces/oils/dressings/condiments, but the most directly cited suppliers, Ventura Foods and Golden State Foods, appear private, so public-market mapping currently routes through distributors and diversified ingredient companies. The universe deliberately includes underfollowed and second-order names, not just restaurant brands. Several names remain hypotheses pending filing-level verification of customer concentration, foodservice revenue purity, contract terms, and market-pricing context.
